about: Clay's body (neck, torso, tail, then limbs and wings), element by element (see body_sheets.md). Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side sheet; x = Clay's left. The bind pose is the side sheet's pose, so the side view can be checked against the sheet directly; the tail's lower run is lifted onto the ground and curls toward the viewer (+x).

trunk.note: Neck, torso and tail are one continuous mass, built as one loft along a curved spine with cross-sections perpendicular to it. Measured on the side sheet (trunk_overlay): the spine was traced through the middle of the body, and at each station the depth to the dorsal outline (top of neck and back, outer edge of the tail curl) and to the ventral outline (throat, chest, belly, inner edge of the tail curl) was measured along the perpendicular. The neck is short and thick, the torso a deep barrel (~0.9 from back to belly), the tail thick (~0.25-0.38) nearly to its tip.

width.note: Half-width = factor * mean depth at the widest level of each section. From the official front-facing art (box set, How to Draw, limited edition): the shoulders are about twice as wide as the neck at its base, but the chest is not a barrel. Its section is a deep keel, widest high up at the shoulders and narrowing toward the breastbone, so the front legs hang close beside it, like a cat's. The belly tucks up into a waist before the haunches. The tail is taller than it is wide.

zones.note: On the neck and torso the zone edges are measured side-view lines, not fractions. The dark edge is the line of small square plates: from behind the ear it runs back and then straight DOWN the side of the neck into the shoulder, round the bottom of the dark shoulder patch, and back along the wing arm. The cream edge bounds the wide throat band, down the front of the neck into the chest; behind the forelegs the cream rises to meet the dark edge (no orange band). On the tail (after lines_until_s) the edges are side fractions.

tail_pose.note: the sheet draws the tail's lower run below the feet (it lies nearer the viewer); in 3D it rests on the ground and curls toward the viewer

bones.note: spine bones by ranges of s; the head bone attaches to the last neck bone

keel.note: How much the section narrows from its widest level toward the underside (0 none, 0.5 to half width at the breastbone): the deep keel of the chest, a gentler one under the belly, none on the tail.

front_leg.note: Measured on the side sheet's near front leg (crop px 300-720, py 300-880). The dark shoulder patch is the shoulder blade and its muscles seen from the side; the shoulder joint sits at the front of the upper arm under it (px 425, py 495). The upper arm slopes down and back to an elbow at the bottom of the chest (px 625, py 605; its point at 649, 613); the forearm angles down and forward to a slim wrist (px 515, py 790, 0.155 deep against 0.37 below the elbow); the hand lies flat on the ground. Like a great cat's: the elbow tucked in against the chest, the leg hanging close beside the keel of the chest. Built as bones and muscles (anatomy).

hind_leg.note: Measured on the side sheet (tail crop): the hind leg is drawn in a deep crouch. The thigh, mostly hidden behind the wing, runs down from the hip to a low knee (~px 895, py 720); the shin runs back to the heel near the ground (~px 1090, py 812), cream down its back; the long digitigrade foot runs forward from the heel along the ground to the ball of the foot (~px 900) with dark square studs along its top; four longer, splayed toes with claws; a spur claw at the heel points back. The haunch, from the official art (How to Draw, limited edition): a big rounded orange mass over the folded thigh, growing out of the hips and the root of the tail. Built as bones and muscles (anatomy), like a sitting great cat's, with a reptile's caudofemoralis tying the thigh to the tail.

carapace.note: The dark back is not paint: like the head's roof it is a shell fitted over the trunk, standing proud of it, a turtle-shell carapace. Transverse bands (~0.09-0.12 apart on the sheet) wrap over the top down to the rim; the rim is a row of small square marginal scutes along the measured dark edge, their outer edges rolled outward like a turtle shell's margin. It runs from behind the head down the tail.

anatomy.note: Clay's body is built from the inside out: a skeleton of bones, muscles laid over it from origin to insertion, and one skin over everything (skin.py), so the shoulders grow out of the chest and back, and the haunches out of the hips and the tail. Quadruped anatomy as in a great cat (lion, tiger) for the legs; a reptile's tail root (caudofemoralis, as in lizards and dinosaurs); bird- and dinosaur-like feet. Left side; the right is mirrored. Each piece: from and to (model units), radii [out, across] where 'out' is measured along the hint direction (default: out from the body, +x), the blend radius k with its neighbours, the rig bones that move it, and its colour zone (0 dark, 0.5 orange, 1 cream; null takes the trunk's zone there). Bones show orange where they lie near the skin (the shin, the elbow, the wrist).

muscles.name: shoulder cap: supraspinatus, infraspinatus and deltoid
muscles.why: the dark rounded shoulder patch on the side sheet (px 400-567, py 300-521); How to Draw's rounded shoulder at the top of the near leg

muscles.name: triceps
muscles.why: the heavy upper-arm mass behind the humerus, from the shoulder blade to the point of the elbow (side sheet)

muscles.name: biceps and brachialis
muscles.why: the front of the upper arm under the shoulder point (side sheet)

muscles.name: pectoral
muscles.why: ties the inside of the upper arm to the breastbone, so the leg grows out of the chest (TDP limited-edition cover: the arm's front edge runs on from the chest)

muscles.name: latissimus dorsi
muscles.why: a flat sheet from the back to the upper arm, filling behind the shoulder blade

muscles.name: forearm extensors
muscles.why: the front of the forearm: thick below the elbow, tapering to the slim wrist (side sheet)

muscles.name: forearm flexors
muscles.why: the back of the forearm, cream on the side sheet from below the elbow to the wrist

muscles.name: hand (metacarpals)
muscles.why: a compact, broad, flat hand on the ground (side sheet)

muscles.name: gluteals
muscles.why: the round top of the haunch, growing out of the hips (How to Draw)

muscles.name: quadriceps
muscles.why: the front of the thigh, down to the knee (How to Draw's haunch)

muscles.name: hamstrings (biceps femoris)
muscles.why: the round back of the haunch, from the ischium to the top of the shin

muscles.name: caudofemoralis
muscles.why: a reptile's (and dinosaur's) great tail muscle, from the tail's root to the thigh: the tail and haunch are one mass

muscles.name: adductors
muscles.why: the inside of the thigh, tied to the belly

muscles.name: calf (gastrocnemius)
muscles.why: the back of the shin, cream on the side sheet, to the heel

muscles.name: shin front (tibialis cranialis)
muscles.why: the front of the shin, orange on the side sheet, from below the knee to the ankle

muscles.name: foot (metatarsals)
muscles.why: the long digitigrade foot lying along the ground (side sheet), as in birds and dinosaurs
